ops.title: capt-hook: async store-tier migration to cc-transcript >=14.5
ops.description:
cc-transcript 14.5.0 (2026-07-19) flipped the entire FeedbackStore tier to async — `open`/`close`/`sql`/`execute`/`record_verdict`/`unjudged`/`judged`/`file_mtimes`/`record_file_scan`, `transaction` (async CM), and all of `judge.similar` are coroutines. capt-hook's review stack is sync end-to-end (deliberately, since 9.31.0's v14 migration), so the fix-the-primitive wave (2026-07-19) pinned `cc-transcript[judge]>=14.4,<14.5` — 14.4.0 is the last sync release and carries the wave's primitives (`synthetic_user_event`, degraded-call `error` fields).

Lifting the `<14.5` cap means rearchitecting `ReviewStore` (freshly rebuilt on 14.2's `StoreSchema` composition in the same wave) plus its callers — scan/judge/announce/dashboard/cli — and ~10 test files to async. Check first whether upstream keeps the async direction (14.2.0's CHANGELOG had explicitly gone sync; 14.5.0 reversed under the codex-parsing wave — the sibling session's motivation may inform whether a sync facade returns in 14.6+, which would make this task a no-op pin lift).

ops.text: Pin cap <14.5 lifted and lock resolves latest cc-transcript
Review stack (store/scan/judge/announce/dashboard/cli) green on the async store tier, or upstream restored a sync facade and the cap lift needed no rearchitecture
The pyproject pin comment referencing this task removed
